messages:
anya: quick note from the int4-hybrid canary runs: we see deterministic token misalignment only when role messages flip across KV page boundaries. reproducible at ~20k tokens on long-chat traces :thinking:
liam: only int4? any diffs on int8/float?
anya: float32 and int8 look fine. int4-hybrid triggers an off-by-one-ish shift in top-k after page compaction.

nora: can you paste the minimal repro?
anya: sure. short log:

anya: ```
# tool: ./ci/replay_longchat --model magnet16b-int4-hybrid --trace long_customer_sim --seed=7
[init] kv_window=65536 page_size=8192 ropescale=auto
[priming] 0..1024 system
[priming] 1025..1536 user
[priming] 1537..2048 assistant
...
[compact] page_swap idx=1->2 boundary=8192
[gen] token_idx=19648 expected="service" got="servic�"   <-- wobble starts here
[diag] last_rope_phase=0.00342 rot_idx=19648 pack_stride=4
```

pat: "servic�" is a classic sign of bit corruption or wrong phase application. do we have checksums for packed pages?
liam: we do CRC pages but not per-slot fingerprint. could add a small high-res fingerprint for first/last 16 slots on flip.

ci-bot: ci/canary magnet16b-int4-hybrid: 1 flaky run detected, creating ticket CAN-317000.

anya: hypothesis: when writes from different roles interleave, the page compactor packs slots with a stride that depends on current page offset. int4 pack rounding + rotary index modulo arithmetic injects a micro-phase that isn't preserved across compaction -> misapplied rotary during subsequent attention.
nora: does the runtime re-initialize rotary phase on page load? I thought it was stateless and derived from global position.
anya: it is derived, but we use a per-page "base_pos" that gets updated on compact. if base_pos rounding is truncated to int32 (instead of int64) badness can creep in over long contexts.

liam: small experiment: run int4-hybrid with forced base_pos64 and with pack_stride forced to 1 to rule out packing alignment.

anya: did a quick smoke: base_pos64 + pack_stride=1 pushed divergence out to >120k tokens. so two factors: truncation + pack stride.
pat: nice find. can we also compare hidden-state fingerprints against float32 replay to see which layer diverges first?

anya: set up a shadow replay job that records per-layer cosine similarity of hidden states (float32 vs int4-shadow) and per-attention-phase difference. job id=shadow-317000-rotarycheck. initial output: layer 6 attention phase deviates first, then hidden state divergence cascades.

nora: that points to rotary application mismatch earlier in the stack. add instrumentation that logs rotary phase offsets at page flip and after compaction.

anya: added small dump in kv_compactor: DumpSlotFingerprints(page->id, /*n=*/16); LogBasePos64(page->id, base_pos64);

liam: please also add a unit test that alternates role writes across a small page boundary repeatedly to try to trigger the bug quickly. make it part of nightly-int4-smoke.

pat: I'll schedule the grid: pack_stride={1,2,4} base_pos_type={int32,int64} ropescale={auto,1.0} page_size={4096,8192} on runner:ci-gpu-xlarge. ETA 10h for initial heatmap.

ci-bot: deploy/canary patch: anya/kv-fingerprint-dump -> queued for canary staging.

anya: action items summary:
- anya: push compactor dumps + base_pos64 patch to canary (ETA 1h)
- liam: add unit test to repo and nightly (ETA EOD)
- pat: run grid and share heatmap here (ETA 10h)
- nora: instrument delayed rotational phase check in attention kernels (ETA 4h)

liam: FYI I created ticket ML-3910 to track this for int4 onboarding. marking P1 until we see a clean fix.

anya: storing artifacts s3://redwood-ml/canaries/3170002222/ (fingerprints, page-dumps, heatmap link when available).

pat: starting grid now. will dump interim heatmap at ~40% progress.

nora: if base_pos64 fixes most cases we should backport defensively to other quant paths. don't want production surprises.

anya: agreed. thanks team. will keep updates here and paste logs/links as soon as canary finishes. :rocket:
